html:
The oldest complete Chinese book on farming, written by the official Jia Sixie and finished in about 544, under the Northern Wei and its successor states. Its title means "Essential techniques for the welfare of the people".

Jia came from Shandong, a major grain region. His book covers ploughing and sowing millet, wheat and beans, fruit trees, silkworms, raising horses, cattle and sheep, and a great deal of food craft: brewing wine, making vinegar and soy sauce, pickling and cooking. He quoted almost two hundred older books, many now lost, so the text also saves earlier farming knowledge.

It was written for the dry north, where farmers had to keep moisture in the soil. The book shows how much of Chinese cooking and fermentation was already in place by the 6th century. Later manuals of the Song and Ming built on it, and it is still read by historians of food and farming, as is the Roman Cato on farming in the West.
sum: The oldest complete Chinese book on farming, written by the official Jia Sixie and finished in about 544, under the Northern Wei and its successor states. Its title means "Essential techniques for the welfare of the people".
